subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: TORCH, Rubella, Toxoplasmosis, CMV and Varicella

steps.tx: The congenital infection group screened by the TORCH acronym covers **TORCH** infections. Toxoplasma, rubella, cytomegalovirus and herpes overlap in causing growth restriction and brain injury. Routine TORCH panels after one miscarriage are discouraged without specific indication. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: TORCH infections overlap in causing growth restriction and brain injury in the fetus.

steps.tx: First trimester rubella infection causing cataract, deafness and heart defects is **congenital rubella** syndrome. Risk exceeds eighty percent in the first twelve weeks and falls sharply after. Immunity is checked at booking and vaccination given after delivery if susceptible. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Congenital rubella syndrome follows first trimester infection with cataract, deafness and heart defects.

steps.tx: Parasite infection from undercooked meat and cat litter requiring spiramycin treatment is **toxoplasmosis**, treated with spiramycin to reduce transmission. Pyrimethamine combinations treat confirmed fetal infection after amniocentesis. Transmission rises with gestation while severity falls. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Toxoplasmosis uses spiramycin to reduce transmission, with severity falling as gestation rises.

steps.tx: The commonest congenital viral infection, mostly silent at birth, is **cytomegalovirus**. Symptomatic babies show growth restriction, microcephaly and periventricular calcification. Hearing loss may appear later in initially silent cases, so audiology follows known infections. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Cytomegalovirus is the commonest congenital viral infection and can cause later hearing loss.

steps.tx: Chickenpox in pregnancy risking severe maternal pneumonia and fetal varicella syndrome is **varicella** infection. Immunoglobulin after exposure protects susceptible women when given promptly. Aciclovir treats established maternal disease. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Varicella risks maternal pneumonia and fetal syndrome, with immunoglobulin after exposure.

steps.tx: IgM positivity alone overdiagnoses acute infection because it persists and cross reacts, a **serology pitfall**. Avidity testing dates rubella and toxoplasma infections helpfully. Reference laboratory confirmation precedes irreversible decisions. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Serology pitfalls mean IgM alone overdiagnoses, and avidity testing dates infections.

steps.tx: Parvovirus B19 causing fetal anaemia and hydrops through red cell aplasia is monitored by **MCA Doppler surveillance**. Intrauterine transfusion rescues hydropic fetuses dramatically. Most maternal infections, however, end with healthy babies. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Parvovirus causes fetal anaemia monitored by MCA Doppler and rescued by transfusion.

steps.tx: Syphilis, though not in the classic acronym, outranks most TORCH agents in preventability, screened as **syphilis screening**. Penicillin in pregnancy cures mother and fetus together. Rising rates make booking screening non negotiable. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Syphilis screening with penicillin treatment cures mother and fetus together.

steps.tx: Counselling after a positive screen must separate transmission risk from damage risk, termed **risk communication**. Many positive mothers deliver uninfected, undamaged babies. Specialist fetal medicine input prevents both panic and complacency. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Risk communication separates transmission chance from damage chance after positive screens.
